The package requires **mgcv** 1.9-3 or later. The table reflects regression tests
and targeted fitting checks on mgcv 1.9-3 through 1.9-5. **Tested** denotes a
route exercised by the package regression suite. **Checked** denotes a route
exercised on a smooth-model fixture. A dash denotes an unavailable route.
The checks use free smoothing parameters and verify the criterion that actually ran.

¹ An NCV deletion for `gpdlss()` can move a held-out excess outside the fitted
support. Such a trial has infinite score. QNCV uses a local quadratic
approximation around the full-data predictors.

² Estimated dispersion can make the outer NCV or QNCV optimization sensitive
to the dataset for `gpoisson()`. Check `fit$outer.info$conv` as well as
`fit$converged` and any warnings.

³ These four single-predictor families reject GAM NCV and QNCV on mgcv 1.9-4.
These entries are for mgcv 1.9-5. See the version qualification below.

Ordinary `bam()` also accepts `GCV.Cp`, `GACV.Cp`, `P-REML`, and `P-ML`.
At fixed unit scale the first two use UBRE and the Pearson likelihood
criteria reduce to REML and ML. Use `scale = 1` for absolute likelihood
comparisons. Check `fit$method` and `fit$dinfo` to see which criterion
and fitter ran. Ordinary BAM requests for NCV enable discretization.
Discrete fitting is available for fREML and NCV, including NCV on mgcv 1.9-3.

## Extended generalized Pareto optimizers

The following smoothing-selection routes for `egpdlss()` were checked with
mgcv 1.9-5. All fits used at least one free smoothing parameter.

| Entry point | Criterion | Newton | BFGS | EFS |
|:--|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `gam()` | REML | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `gam()` | NCV | No | Yes | No |
| `gam()` | QNCV | No | Yes | No |
| `scasm()` | REML | No | No | Yes |
| `scasm()` | NCV | No | No | No |
| `scasm()` | QNCV | No | No | No |

- For NCV and QNCV, `estimate.gam()` always selects outer BFGS. For QNCV
  it also sets the family's quadratic approximation flag. The returned
  `fit$optimizer` can echo the original request even after the switch.
  Use `optimizer = c("outer", "bfgs")` to make the call match the fit.
  Exact NCV can have an infinite score if an approximate deletion prediction
  places a held-out response beyond the fitted upper endpoint, and BFGS
  can fail if its starting score is infinite. QNCV evaluates a local
  quadratic approximation to the likelihood.
- In REML, the general-family branch supplies no objective scaling value to
  `gam.outer()`. Its additional `nlm` and `optim` routes fail in mgcv 1.9-5
  with free smoothing parameters, before an inlaws callback can supply that
  value. EFS with free smoothing parameters uses mgcv's general-family
  `efsud()`. Inlaws requires all smoothing parameters to be free and unlinked,
  or all fixed. With all smoothing parameters fixed, no optimizer is needed.
- `scasm()` calls `scasm.fit()` directly. It uses constrained Newton updates
  for coefficients and EFS updates for the smoothing parameters, and reports
  a Laplace REML score. It has no method, neighbourhood or outer optimizer
  argument, and silently ignores those named arguments in `...` in 1.9-5.
  General-family hooks supply likelihoods and initial values. There is no
  hook for replacing the smoothing loop or evaluating a deletion criterion
  in that loop. Monotone smooths with binding inequalities were tested.
  A smooth with zero free directions after all its constraints bind can
  fail in the mgcv 1.9-5 covariance projection. This also occurs with
  built-in mgcv families.
- `gpdlss()` is the canonical name for the original two-predictor GPD.
  `gpd()` remains an alias. Use `egpdlss()` for a third predictor for bulk
  shape. The new family uses separate coefficient blocks for its predictors.

The regression tests in `tests/egpdlss-fits.R` record actual optimizer calls
and the criterion, including the QNCV flag.

## Qualifications

- **Hyper-Poisson predictors:** `hyper_poissonls()` models the exact mean and
  dispersion with log links, offsets and shared coefficients. REML supports
  Newton, BFGS and EFS; NCV/QNCV use BFGS. EFS requires all smoothing parameters
  free and unlinked, or all fixed, and uses gamma one. The native CDF, quantile,
  simulation and gratia diagnostic callbacks describe the response distribution.
  The shared missing-row neighbourhood guard applies; on mgcv 1.9-4 fully
  unpenalized NCV/QNCV models require explicit `nei` with `jackknife = FALSE`.
  Dispersion one gives Poisson; finite dispersion has a restricted variance
  range at fixed mean and boundary estimates can be weakly identified.
  Tests are in `tests/hyper-poisson-*.R`.
- **Beta mean and precision:** `betals()` uses two formulae for logit mean
  and log precision, with smooths and offsets in both. Responses must be
  strictly inside `(0, 1)`. It supports REML Newton/BFGS and NCV, including
  grouped neighbourhoods; QNCV and shared coefficients are unsupported.
  Response columns are `mu`, `phi`, with variance `mu * (1 - mu) / (1 + phi)`.
  Tests are in `tests/betals.R` and `tests/betals-derivatives.R`.
- **General families:** mgcv fits these families with `gam()`. An ML
  request falls back to REML. Requests for GCV, GACV, Pearson
  likelihood criteria, or fREML also fall back to REML for the families
  above. Check the criterion in `fit$method`.
- **Optimizers:** `zoibetals()` and `dirmult()` use extended Fellner--Schall (`optimizer =
  "efs"`), selected automatically; Newton/BFGS smoothing optimization is not
  implemented. `betabinomial()` has tested REML Newton and BFGS routes;
  `nbls()`, `zinb()`, and `zanb()` also have tested EFS routes. NCV for
  `zinb()` and `zanb()` uses BFGS, not EFS.
- **NCV and QNCV:** NCV uses approximate neighbourhood deletions.
  `betabinomial()` deletes entire rows of aggregated binomial counts.
  The general-family scores and gradients align offsets with prediction
  rows. Discrete `bam()` NCV uses the working linear model, so its
  optimum can differ from `gam()` NCV.
- **mgcv 1.9-4 GAM NCV restriction:** `cgamma()`, `clognormal()`, `cmp()`,
  and `gpoisson()` reject GAM NCV, QNCV, and REML with `nei` on this version
  because of independent upstream numerical issues. The two censored
  families also lose censoring information in held-out response subsetting.
  In mgcv 1.9-3, the native extended-family GAM NCV code can omit held-out
  offsets and lose censoring attributes. The four-family GAM NCV/QNCV
  entries refer to mgcv 1.9-5.
  On mgcv 1.9-5 the methods run on smooth-model fixtures. Estimated
  generalized Poisson dispersion can still give a step-failure diagnostic on
  some datasets. Discrete BAM NCV is subject to the preprocessing
  qualification below.
- **Fixed likelihood scale:** use `scale = 1` for absolute `bam()` likelihood
  comparisons with these four extended families: mgcv 1.9-4 can mislabel the
  default fixed external scale. This is separate from estimated dispersion.
- **Censored location-scale families:** `cgammals()` and `clognormalls()`
  use two formulae and support REML, NCV, and QNCV, including grouped neighbourhoods
  and offsets in both predictors. `cgammals()` returns mean and dispersion
  (`mu`, `phi`), with variance `phi * mu^2`; `clognormalls()` returns mean and
  log-response standard deviation (`mu`, `sigma`). Both use ordinary log links
  and require separate coefficients for the two predictors. A constant second
  predictor need not reproduce REML estimates from `cgamma()` or `clognormal()`.
- **ML edge cases:** in mgcv 1.9-4, entirely unpenalized `gam(method = "ML")`
  models can hit a native solver limitation with `gpoisson()` or the cauchit link
  of `cumulative_link()`. Smooth-model ML is supported; see the family help pages
  for alternatives.
- **Poisson inverse Gaussian predictors:** `pigls()` uses separate
  log-linked predictors for mean and dispersion and returns `mu` and
  `theta`, with variance `mu + theta * mu^2`. REML uses outer Newton or
  BFGS and NCV and QNCV use BFGS. A constant dispersion predictor need
  not reproduce REML estimates from `pig()`.
- **CMP predictors:** `cmpls()` models the exact mean and dispersion with
  separate log-link predictors in `gam()`, with REML, NCV, and QNCV support.
  Use two formulae; `~ 1` estimates constant dispersion. See `?cmpls` for
  numerical limits and supported prediction and distribution callbacks.
- **Weibull predictors:** Both families model the arithmetic mean of a positive,
  uncensored response. `weibulls()` uses two log-linked predictors for mean
  and shape. In `gam()`, REML uses Newton, BFGS or EFS, and NCV/QNCV use BFGS.
  With mgcv 1.9-4 and 1.9-5, `scasm()` supports constrained REML via its
  EFS loop. Its interface and implementation provide no NCV/QNCV route.
  If all directions of a smooth are constrained, its EFS penalty trace can
  fail on the empty projected penalty.
  General-family `nlm` and `optim` dispatch fails in those mgcv versions
  because the null-model objective scale is unset.
  `weibull()` uses a single log-mean predictor and a fixed or estimated global
  shape. In `gam()`, REML uses Newton, BFGS, `nlm`, `optim` or EFS, and ML
  uses Newton with positive weights. Omit zero-weight rows before `gam()` ML on mgcv through
  1.9-5 because of its extended-family ML penalty path. GAM NCV/QNCV use BFGS
  even when mgcv retains the requested optimizer in the result. Ordinary `bam()` uses outer Newton for
  REML/ML and performance iteration with Newton for fREML. Discrete fREML/NCV
  use Cholesky-based performance iteration. Discrete NCV uses the working-model
  neighbourhood criterion. In `bam()`, specify `scale = 1` to correct scale
  and `logLik()` reporting on mgcv 1.9-4 and 1.9-5. See
  `tests/weibull-models.R` for fitting, criteria, predictions, and diagnostics.
- **Log-logistic predictors:** `log_logistic()` models arithmetic mean with a
  log link and estimates or fixes a global logistic scale for `log(Y)`.
  `log_logisticls()` uses log/logit links for mean and varying scale, with
  two formulae and separate coefficients. Both constrain scale to `(0, 1)`;
  variance is infinite at scale >= 0.5, where Pearson residuals are `NA`.
  Tests are in `tests/log-logistic-models.R` and `tests/log-logisticls.R`.
- **Student-t predictors:** `scatlss(min.df = 3)` models location, scale
  and df with identity, log and shifted-log links. Use three formulae;
  `~ 1` in the third estimates global df. Finite `min.df > 2` retains finite
  response variance `sigma^2 * nu / (nu - 2)`; scale is not the standard
  deviation. REML Newton/BFGS and NCV/QNCV BFGS, including grouped
  neighbourhoods and offsets, are tested on mgcv 1.9-4. The numeric response
  avoids the extended-family attribute-loss defect, including when NCV is
  requested via `nei` during REML. Signed-Hessian CG deletion solves and local
  score/gradient and jackknife assembly address separate upstream NCV issues.
  The shared neighbourhood-preprocessing guard described below also applies
  to `scatlss()`, preserving valid whole-group omissions and default
  leave-one-out after omission. Guard rejections are separate from numerical
  and successful end-to-end validation.
  Fully unpenalized NCV/QNCV requires explicit `nei` with `jackknife = FALSE`:
  a separate mgcv 1.9-4 empty-penalty reparameterization defect blocks its
  jackknife covariance; criterion evaluation and unpenalized REML are supported.
  Large df and varying scale/tail weight can be weakly identified. No future
  mgcv fix is assumed. Tests are in `tests/scatlss-*.R`.
- **Blended GEV predictors:** `bgevlss()` models a location quantile,
  positive quantile spread and positive tail shape with identity, log and
  log links. Verified GAM routes on mgcv 1.9-3 to 1.9-5 and constrained
  `scasm()` on 1.9-4 and 1.9-5.

  | Fitter | REML | NCV | QNCV |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `gam()` | Newton, BFGS, EFS | BFGS | BFGS |
  | `scasm()` with a monotone smooth | EFS | Unavailable | Unavailable |

  The `scasm()` fitter hardwires REML/EFS, including for a smooth with
  binding inequalities. Its public interface has no criterion or optimizer
  selector and has no neighbourhood deletion path. The 1.9-5 fitter can
  fail in covariance projection when a smooth has no free coefficient
  directions and fails at setup when no smooth is present.
  The `gam()` routes use the same signed-Hessian NCV compatibility code
  as `scatlss()`. The upstream unpenalized jackknife limitation affects
  mgcv 1.9-3 and 1.9-4.
  `gam()` EFS requires unlinked free penalties or entirely fixed penalties.
  mgcv leaves the outer objective scale unset for general families, which
  prevents REML smoothing selection with its `nlm` and `optim` optimizers.
  NCV and QNCV dispatch to BFGS.
  Response mean and variance require shape < 1 and < 0.5, respectively.
  See `tests/bgevlss-*.R` for distribution and fitting checks.
- **Generalized gamma predictors:** `gen_gammalss()` and its censored counterpart
  `cgen_gammalss()` model arithmetic mean,
  Prentice scale and transformed shape with three log-linked predictors.
  Response columns are `mu`, `sigma`, `r`, where `r = 1 + sigma * Q > 0`
  enforces a finite mean. Constant `r` does not imply constant `Q` when
  scale varies. Variance requires `r > 0.5`. REML uses Newton or BFGS;
  NCV/QNCV use BFGS and mgcv 1.9-4 conjugate-gradient deletion solves.
  Jackknife coefficient updates are computed locally. Reassess these
  compatibility measures after upstream NCV fixes in later mgcv versions.
  The censored family accepts the same response encoding as `cgamma()`,
  supports all three predictor offsets, and integrates analytic derivatives
  through order four for censoring probabilities, including at `Q = 0`.
- **Ordered beta predictions:** `predict(fit, type = "response")` now returns
  five columns ordered `mu`, `p0`, `pI`, `p1`, `mean`: the interior beta mean,
  zero/interior/one probabilities, and complete mean `p1 + pI * mu`.
  This replaces the previous complete-mean vector; use column 5 or
  `predict_ordbeta(fit)` for that vector. The helper restores names mgcv may
  discard and also selects `"conditional"` and `"probabilities"`. Standard errors
  use coefficient covariance with fitted precision and active cutpoints fixed;
  `unconditional = TRUE` requests smoothing uncertainty correction only.
  Disabled endpoints have exactly zero probability and standard error.
  Link predictions remain `eta`, and `fitted.values` remains the interior mean
  required by distribution callbacks. Tests are in `tests/ordbeta.R`.
- **Inflated beta:** `zoibetals(inflation = "both")` uses four formulas:
  interior logit mean, log precision, zero logit, one logit. `"zero"` and
  `"one"` use three formulas, fixing the excluded probability to zero.
  Endpoint logits use the interior as reference. REML uses EFS with all-free
  unlinked or all-fixed smoothing parameters; shared smoothing IDs and partly
  fixed penalties are rejected. Active but unobserved components are rejected.
  `predict_zoibetals()` exposes interior parameters, all component
  probabilities, and complete response moments. Native callbacks consume link
  predictor matrices; diagnostics provide endpoint left limits for randomized
  PIT. Deviance diagnostics are undefined; use response, Pearson or quantile
  residuals. Tests are in `tests/zoibetals.R`; a comparison with `ordbeta()`
  is in `inst/examples/zoibetals.R`.
- **Inflated and hurdle negative binomial:** `zinb()` and `zanb()` keep three
  fitted-value columns (`mu`, `p`, `theta`). Native `predict(type = "response")`
  returns those three followed by the complete `mean`, `variance`, and `p0`
  (actual zero probability). mgcv can drop column names, so use positions 4:6
  for these additional quantities. `se.fit = TRUE` uses the delta method with
  the full coefficient covariance, including shared coefficients;
  `unconditional = TRUE` requests smoothing-parameter uncertainty when available.
  These are estimation errors, not predictive standard deviations. Pass the
  first three columns to the distribution callbacks. Prediction tests are in
  `tests/zinb-prediction.R`; the inventory and decisions for all families are in
  `inst/maths/family-prediction-audit.md` in the package source.
- **Scope:** `cmp()` is a pure-R reference implementation whose large-data
  performance is unvalidated. No family here has a supported `gamm()` route.

## Explicit neighbourhoods and missing observations

In mgcv 1.9-4, `gam()` and `bam()` call the shared `nanei()` helper after
model-frame omission when `nei` is supplied. Partial removals can leave the
cumulative boundaries `ma` and `md` unchanged. If an index set contains no
omitted row, a separate negative-subscript error can empty that set. This
affects deletion sets, prediction sets, or both, including different subsets
and reordered or repeated predictions. It is a preprocessing defect, separate
from held-out response attributes, signed-curvature deletion updates, QNCV
scores/offsets and unpenalized jackknife covariance.

`betabinomial()`, `betals()`, `cgammals()`, `clognormalls()`, `cmpls()`,
`pigls()`, `log_logisticls()`, `gen_gammalss()`, `cgen_gammalss()`, `scatlss()`,
`egpdlss()`, `zinb()`, `zanb()`, `weibulls()`, `bgevlss()`, `gpdlss()`,
`dirichlet()`, `nbls()`, and `hyper_poissonls()` install a shared
check in the `gam()` general-family `presetup` hook.
It rejects inconsistent adjusted neighbourhoods before upstream validation
and numerical NCV, including explicit NCV, QNCV and `nei` during REML. Each
family's independent method restrictions still apply. The check tests the
adjusted structure on any installed mgcv version; it does not presume a future
release fixes the defect. It does not reconstruct or change neighbourhoods.

There are limits to interception through supported family hooks:

- Extended families have no `gam()` `presetup` hook. Neighbourhood validation
  precedes `preinitialize`, `initialize` and link-fixing callbacks. This affects
  otherwise supported `pig()`, `log_logistic()`, `weibull()` and `cumulative_link()` GAM
  routes, and can preempt the independent GAM NCV rejection for `cgamma()`,
  `clognormal()`, `cmp()` and `gpoisson()`.
- `bam()` also calls `nanei()`, but validates explicit NCV neighbourhoods
  before family hooks. Its supported extended-family discrete NCV routes have
  the same interception limit. General families do not support `bam()`;
  `gam(discrete = TRUE)` constructs a BAM setup and has the same early limit.
- An incomplete `nei` list with omitted observations can fail inside `nanei()`
  itself, before any family hook. A generic upstream error in any of these
  cases is **not** successful inlaws guard coverage. There is no supported
  early family hook to add an informative inlaws error on these routes without
  intrusive coupling to mgcv internals.

For all otherwise supported routes, the reliable workaround is to apply
subset selection and remove incomplete observations using **all** relevant
response, predictor, offset and weight variables, then construct `nei` using
the resulting data's row indices. Merely supplying neighbourhoods indexed to
complete cases while leaving incomplete rows in the fitting data still invokes
the faulty preprocessing. `subset` is applied before omission; explicit indices
must refer to the selected data, not the original unselected rows.

Complete-data grouped neighbourhoods and default leave-one-out (`nei = NULL`)
constructed after omission remain supported. Whole-group removals that produce
correct neighbourhoods are permitted. Ordinary REML without `nei` is unaffected.
Fitting a precomputed `G` does not run `nanei()` again: construct any new `nei`
against `G`'s retained rows. Ordering, repetitions and separate deletion and
prediction sets keep their existing meaning.

`tests/ncv-neighbourhoods.R` checks independent expected contents and boundaries,
the public `gam()` integration, successful supported fits, independent guard
preservation, and the interception limits separately. The source audit in
`inst/maths/ncv-neighbourhood-audit.md` records hook ordering and the shared
`scatlss()` integration. Its separate signed-deletion, QNCV and jackknife
numerical checks are in `tests/scatlss-ncv.R`.

For a conservative starting point, use `gam(..., method = "REML")` with the
family's documented formula structure. For large-data fitting, the tested
choices are `cgamma()`, `clognormal()`, `cumulative_link()`, and `pig()` with
`bam(..., method = "fREML")`, with or without discretization. Consult each
family's help for response encoding, links, parameter constraints, and
prediction semantics; a **Yes** here is not a guarantee of convergence for
every dataset.

The evidence for each row is in the correspondingly named test file (for
example, `tests/cgamma.R`); ordinal tests are in `tests/cumulative-link.R`,
zero-inflated and hurdle tests in `tests/zinb-models.R` and `tests/zinb-ncv.R`,
Poisson inverse Gaussian checks in `tests/pig-models.R`, `tests/pigls-models.R`
and `tests/pigls-ncv.R`,
and additional NCV checks in `tests/clognormal-ncv.R` and
`tests/betabinomial-smoothing.R`. Update this table when adding fitting routes
or extending their validation.

The four extended-family rows above are additionally covered by
`tests/extended-family-routes.R` and `tests/extended-family-ncv.R`, including
fixed and estimated dispersion, offsets, case weights, family reuse, likelihood
statistics, independent distribution limits and explicit NCV rejection under mgcv 1.9-4.
